newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Deputies say too early to make Kazakh leader a hero.
newsitem.headline: Deputies say too early to make Kazakh leader a hero.

text.p: In a rare display of defiance, Kazakh parliamentary deputies on Monday threw out a proposal to make the former Soviet republic's president, Nursultan Nazarbayev, a "people's hero".
The proposal from one deputy to make Nazarbayev a "khalik kakharmany", or people's hero, was dismissed by deputies on a technicality, saying it was not on the day's order of business.
But several deputies told the chamber that the oil-rich republic's economic hardships meant it was too early to grant the country's former Communist Party boss the award.
"It would be blasphemy to grant such an award with the economic situation as it is," opposition deputy Zamanbek Nurkadilov told Reuters. "The award would simply lose its value."
Little has changed politically in most Central Asian republics since Soviet times, and leaders such as Nazarbayev wield strong executive powers and brook little opposition.
But a backlog of unpaid salaries and pensions, energy shortages and high prices have tried the patience of Kazakhstan's 16.9 million population.
